title: Gaussian Splatting-based Volumetric Video Compression with Sparse 4D Anchors
claim: Sparse hierarchical anchors and a long-context entropy model give far smaller representations at higher quality than flat-anchor and prior baselines.
layout: 4-panel 2x2 image grid left, rate-distortion plots right, diagonal split in (a)
description: The left side is a 2x2 grid of renderings of a kitchen scene with a person cooking and a dog. Panel (a) is split diagonally. The left half is 4D Scaffold GS (31.7 dB, 247 MB) and the right half is SAGA (34.5 dB, 1.91 MB coded). Panel (b) shows flat 4D anchors as a dense cloud of colored dots, with a 32-d PCA feature colour key. Panel (c) shows hierarchical 4D anchors as a much sparser dot cloud, annotated '30x fewer features than flat anchors'. Panel (d) shows per-anchor required bits as a blue-yellow heatmap of dots, with a colorbar for 1.1 to 4.5 bits per value. On the right, two stacked rate-distortion plots show PSNR and SSIM against size in MB on a log axis. SAGA's purple curve is up and to the left of all baselines, which have distinct markers and a legend.
caption: SAGA: Hierarchical 4D anchors for compact dynamic scenes. While flat 4D anchors (b) store features individually, SAGA (c) concentrates features at sparse coarse-level anchors, achieving a 30× reduction in feature-bearing anchors. Our long-context entropy model further exploits dependencies among features, achieving an average coding rate of just 2 bits/symbol (d). Together, these designs compress a 300-frame Neu3D scene to 1.91MB—129× smaller than 4D Scaffold-GS (a)—while achieving the best rate-distortion trade-off among state-of-the-art baselines (right).
abstract: Immersive video communication requires photorealistic, compact dynamic scene representations that support efficient rendering. 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) is a promising approach, but dynamic 3DGS remains difficult to compress due to its dense primitives and spatiotemporal redundancy. Anchor-based formulations improve compactness through sparse scaffolds that share geometry and appearance across primitives. However, existing designs typically deform a single canonical scaffold and condition each primitive solely on its associated anchor, limiting their ability to model non-local dynamics and disocclusions and exploit inter-anchor correlations. To address these limitations, we propose SAGA, a volumetric video codec built on Sparse Anchor-assisted GAussian splatting representations. SAGA represents a dynamic scene using hierarchical sparse anchors in 4D space-time. Coordinate-based INR decoders generate fine anchors and Gaussian primitives from features obtained through kernel interpolation among nearby anchors, enabling parameter sharing across spatiotemporal structures. A fixed-size memory with a novel orthogonality-informed slot-update strategy further captures long-range dependencies among unstructured anchors for entropy coding. Empirically, \name achieves PSNR-based BD-rate reductions of 90.88%, 64.30% and 65.14% relative to GIFStream, TED-4DGS, and OMG4, respectively, on the Neu3D testset.
